published_statement: NOT QUOTED -- source unreadable in this run (see source.located). What was COMPUTED instead (rederive A,B): on Minkowski spacetime ds^2 = c^2 dt^2 - dx^2, a clock on the inertial worldline x = beta c t accumulates proper time tau = t sqrt(1-beta^2) = t/gamma, gamma = 1/sqrt(1-beta^2); crossing coordinate distance D at constant beta takes t = D/(beta c) and tau = D/(beta gamma c). The boost preserves the interval and a clock at rest in the moving frame reads t' = t/gamma.
published_hypotheses: NOT QUOTED from source. Hypotheses under which the computed statement holds (each needed by the derivation, rederive A-B): H1 flat (Minkowski) spacetime; H2 the reference frame (Earth frame) is inertial; H3 the clock's worldline is inertial at constant beta over the interval (for non-inertial segments the CLOCK HYPOTHESIS, tau = integral sqrt(1-v^2/c^2) dt, is an additional hypothesis); H4 the invariant speed C of the Lorentz group equals the measured light speed c (LSV gr-qc/0107091 p.4, p.10 as quoted by the sibling audit -- 'tiny deviations ... are logically possible').

rederivation.outcome: OVERALL PASS (output in rederive/special-relativity-kinematics.out). A: tau = D/(beta gamma c) from ds^2 exactly. B: boost preserves the interval; moving clock t' = t/gamma; gamma composition g1 g2 (1+b1 b2). C: sqrt((1+b)/(1-b)) = gamma(1+b) on 0<=b<1 (sympy squares + z3 nlsat unsat for a counterexample) -- the arrival.py:71-73 self-check is a true identity. D: (gamma-1)mc^2 = mv^2/2 + 3mv^4/(8c^2) + O(v^6). E: arrival.py numbers reproduced (gamma(0.866)=1.999824; 4.89607 yr; 2.44825 yr; LY and c consistent). F: constant-beta times are strict floors; +59% shipboard at 1 g for 0.866c. G: flat-spacetime term 9.9e-9 at 1 AU. H: times linear in D. I (RECORD, rests_on_it prose vs code, not SR): arrival.py:150-151 says '810 AU' where the code prints 2002 AU for the same inputs; arrival.py:152 says '2.6 ly' where the code prints 0.084 ly; arrival.py:137 says '76x the fuel ratio' where fuel-per-tonne ratio is 56.0, M0/M1 ratio 3.56, ln ratio 27.6 -- 76 not reproduced. These are discrepancies recorded, not repaired, and none is in gamma.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What the 1905 kinematics used: the relativity principle, light-speed invariance and inertial frames -- no numerical datum enters gamma or tau = t/gamma except c itself, now exact by definition. So there is no datum whose later refinement could move the formula; the only data in the tree's use are the destination distance and the proton mass, and both enter linearly with the conclusion insensitive by computation (rederive H). Evidence the other way -- what later data could bear on it: high-precision time-dilation tests and Lorentz-violation searches (NAMED-NOT-READ in this run; nothing about their results is asserted here). The one place a limitation bites is not missing data but a hypothesis the tree's report drops: the constant-beta cruise. Restoring it is computed here (+59% shipboard at 1 g, 0.866c) and cuts against the drive's figure, not for it. Net: on this result M's hypothesis finds no lacked datum; it finds a dropped hypothesis in the use.
grade_evidence: The formula as the tree codes it (arrival.py:29-30, 58-60) is exact under flat spacetime + inertial constant-beta cruise: re-derived symbolically from the Minkowski interval (rederive A,B), identity used as self-check proven (C, sympy+z3), every pinned number reproduced (E). It is narrowed because the tree's report applies the constant-beta shipboard/Earth times to whole trips (arrival.py:133-135) without naming that hypothesis, in a file about the braking manoeuvre: those figures are strict floors (d(beta gamma)/d beta = gamma^3 > 0, rederive F), 59% low at a 1 g profile for the slingshot's 0.866c and 0.05% low for the shell. Not WRONG: no counterexample to the kinematics exists here; the prose-vs-code mismatches at arrival.py:137,150-152 are discrepancies in rests_on_it prose, not in gamma. Caveat carried on the grade: the source and every restatement were unreadable in this run (quota/egress), so the grade rests on computation, not on a quotation.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the report label the times at arrival.py:133-135 as constant-beta cruise floors (as the magsail distances already are), or include the acceleration phases. To OPEN-for-hypotheses: none -- the mathematics is checked; but a reading of Einstein 1905 via a restating arXiv paper (e.g. 1409.7951, gr-qc/0502097) once alphaXiv quota resets should replace the NOT QUOTED statement and confirm H1-H4. To WRONG: an experiment reading showing time dilation departs from 1/sqrt(1-beta^2) at the 1e-3 level at beta <= 0.87 -- none is known to this audit and none was read.
